target_claims: WF-Bench contains target wavefunctions from topological states, Wigner crystals, and superconducting wavefunctions (Figure 1).
The dataset includes 31 target wavefunctions, with F(Ne=8) reported for all included wavefunctions (Figure 3).
The benchmarking protocol optimizes neural wavefunctions against target wavefunctions using negative log fidelity as the matching loss (Section 4).
For nine representative wavefunctions, the paper fits fidelity scaling of the form F = 1 - alpha(Ne - 2)^beta for Ferminet and Psiformer (Figure 4).
Table 1 reports F(8), alpha, beta, and RMSE for Ferminet and Psiformer across the nine representative wavefunctions (Table 1).

target_claims: The paper formalizes randomized self-reduction learning and provides sample-complexity analysis under correlated sampling (Section 4).
RSR-Bench contains 80 benchmark functions for evaluating randomized self-reduction discovery (Section 5).
Vanilla Bitween discovers randomized self-reductions for 43 of 80 RSR-Bench functions, including the first known sigmoid reduction (Table 1).
Agentic Bitween discovers randomized self-reductions for 64 of 80 RSR-Bench functions by letting LLM agents propose query functions beyond the fixed prior query set (Table 1).
On nonlinear invariant benchmarks, the regression backend outperforms the MILP backend in sample count and runtime (Table 2).

target_claims: Success conditioning is proved to exactly solve a trust-region policy optimization problem with a chi-squared divergence constraint whose radius is determined by the data (Section 4.3).
At the optimum, relative policy improvement, chi-squared policy-change magnitude, and action-influence are shown to be exactly equal at every state (Section 4.4).
The analysis characterizes exact success conditioning as a conservative improvement operator that cannot degrade performance or induce dangerous distribution shift (Section 4.3).
The paper analyzes return thresholding as an extension that can amplify improvement but can misalign the learned policy with the true objective (Section 5).

target_claims: RACO is an offline, reward-free preference-alignment method that accepts user-specified objective weights and explicitly handles conflicting objectives (Table 1).
The method uses CAGrad-Clip to limit correction gradients so updates better respect preferred objective trade-offs (Figure 1, Algorithm 1).
On TL;DR summarization, RACO achieves better Pareto frontiers for conciseness-quality and faithfulness-quality trade-offs than AMoPO and weighted-loss DPO baselines (Figure 2, Figure 3).
On BeaverTails safety alignment, RACO improves harmlessness-helpfulness Pareto trade-offs across Qwen3 and Gemma3 setups (Figure 4).
Ablations show clipping and the correction-radius constant affect validation margins and Pareto frontiers (Figure 5, Figure 6).
RACO directly applies conflict-averse gradient descent to objective-specific pairwise preference losses instead of relying on explicit reward models (Section 3).
The clipped CAGrad update is introduced to stabilize multi-objective LLM alignment while respecting user-specified objective weights (Section 3.2).
The paper proves convergence of clipped CAGrad to Pareto-critical points that respect user-specified weights in nonconvex smooth settings (Theorem 3.1).
For two objectives, the analysis shows clipping can strictly improve the convergence rate (Theorem 3.2).
Experiments on multi-objective summarization and safety alignment across Qwen 3, Llama 3, and Gemma 3 report better Pareto trade-offs than reward-free baselines (Section 4).

target_claims: The paper proves DPO-RLHF equivalence is conditional on the RLHF-optimal policy preferring human-preferred responses (Section 3).
When the equivalence assumption fails, DPO optimizes relative advantage over the reference policy rather than absolute human-preference alignment (Section 3).
The paper characterizes undesirable solution spaces in which policies reduce DPO loss while preferring dispreferred responses (Section 3).
Constrained Preference Optimization augments RLHF with constraints and derives a stationary DPO-like loss with an adaptive reference-based margin (Section 4.3).
The paper gives a soft-margin ranking interpretation showing DPO can implement margin ranking with potentially negative targets (Section 5).
Experiments on standard benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance for CPO (Section 6).

target_claims: Mechanistic Data Attribution quantifies individual training-sample influence on targeted interpretable LLM units such as induction and previous-token heads (Figure 1, Table 3).
Targeted deletion or augmentation of high-influence samples causally modulates induction-head and previous-token-head emergence more than random interventions (Figure 2).
High-influence samples for induction heads are concentrated in repetitive structural domains, with top-ranked examples including LaTeX, HTML, and repeated text patterns (Table 1, Figure 4).
Synthetic data patterns selected from Pythia-14M attribution generalize to larger model scales when augmenting induction-head formation (Table 2).
Interventions that alter induction-head strength also shift in-context learning scores, supporting a causal link between the mechanism and ICL behavior (Figure 5).

target_claims: The paper derives prompt steering interventions by subtracting unsteered activations from prompt-steered activations and trains PSR models to approximate successful prompt interventions (Figure 1).
Prompt steering applies highly token-dependent intervention strengths, motivating token-specific activation steering rather than constant coefficients (Figure 2).
PSR models estimate token-specific steering coefficients from activations and are trained with log-likelihood or MSE objectives to imitate prompt steering (Sections 3.4 and 3.5).
On Persona Vectors, all-layer PSR models outperform prompt steering at prompt-steering coherence for all three reported language models (Table 1).
On AxBench Gemma layer subsets, PSR variants improve over several rank-1 activation steering baselines and compare with multi-rank or multi-layer methods (Table 3).
Accumulated PSR interventions have lower relative RMSE to prompt-steering interventions than constant steering on the analyzed Persona Vectors data (Figure 3).

target_claims: DMPO fine-tunes diffusion LLMs by matching the model policy distribution to an optimal reward-tilted distribution through cross-entropy optimization (Section 3).
The method introduces weight baseline subtraction to make small-batch DMPO training effective (Section 3.4).
DMPO is trained without supervised fine-tuning in an R1-Zero-like recipe for reasoning tasks (Section 4).
Across evaluated reasoning benchmarks, DMPO consistently outperforms LLaDA-Instruct, LLaDA-1.5, d1, and cGRPO baselines (Table 1).
DMPO reports accuracy gains up to 54.3% over previous state-of-the-art baselines and 66.41% over the base model (Table 1).

target_claims: The paper argues that vanilla MLP INR low-frequency bias is a symptom of stable-rank degradation during training rather than an intrinsic architectural limitation (Section 3).
Rank-regulating, near-orthogonal Muon updates improve image overfitting quality across multiple INR architectures compared with Adam (Table 1).
Muon improves sparse-view CT reconstruction quality across multiple INR architectures compared with Adam (Table 4).
The reported improvements extend to natural images, medical images, audio, super-resolution, and novel-view synthesis, with up to about +9 dB PSNR over the same architecture (Tables 1-6).
